correctness.rationale: For any generator matrix of the fixed code, every set of k columns is independent, so the check subspace supported on T is the nullspace of the columns in T and has dimension max(|T|−k,0). In particular a (k+1)-set has a one-dimensional check space and every nonzero such check has full support. A cut S with |S|<k would split the rowspace into checks supported on A∪S or B∪S; the sum of their dimensions is less than n−k, whether both, one, or neither contributes a positive dimension. This shows necessity without chordality. A simplicial vertex cannot join different surviving components after fewer than k deletions, because its surviving neighbors form a clique. Repeated deletion therefore gives induced k-connected chordal graphs down to K_{k+1}. At each reverse step a check on the added vertex and k neighbors increases the check rank by one via its nonzero new coordinate; all checks on the smaller graph are exactly checks of the fixed code vanishing off that graph. All edges are covered by (k+1)-cliques inductively, including each edge at the new vertex. The base contributes binom(k+1,2) edges and each step at least k, with equality exactly when all steps have degree k; the resulting k-tree's n−k creation-clique checks are independent by their new coordinates. This includes k=1 and k=n−1. The frozen finite verifier and output were inspected, not executed; its graph loop prefilters on the claimed bound. Independent replay `python3 /workspace/audit_replay.py 2` makes no such prefilter, enumerates graphs and dual vectors for evaluation codes at (n,q)=(4,4),(5,5) for each k, and checks full span and edge agreement on all accepted graphs, with counts (35,7,1) and (541,111,11,1). The proof establishes the all-code and all-field claims.

evidence: The mask result constructs a generalized Reed–Solomon realization subject to expansion and a field-size bound. The MDS treewidth formula is for normal-graph complexity, not edges of a column-primal parity graph. The chordal-code construction supplies particular supports.
broader_coverage.reasoning: None provides an iff criterion for every given code and every labeled chordal target. Simplicial elimination provides the graph extremum independently once the feasible class is known; the coding contribution is to identify that class and realize all equality cases.

evidence: A systematic MDS check matrix with a common k-set in every row gives the split k-tree optimum candidate, and the known chordal code construction gives this kind of example. Support expansion bounds address distance/realization of masks, not the clique-span theorem for an arbitrary fixed code.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: One split equality graph does not imply necessity for every parity-check presentation, realization of arbitrary chordal k-connected graphs, or realization of all k-trees by minimum checks for that same code. The chordal graph extremum has not been credited as an independent novelty.

evidence: The generator matroid is U_{k,n}; a generator-column circuit on each (k+1)-clique supplies a check in the dependency space of a particular representation. Chen et al. give a chordal systematic construction, not a classification of all circuit-supported column-primal graphs.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The genuinely equivalent formulation must concern the dependency space of each representation of U_{k,n} over the given field. A support-pattern existence theorem or a generic representation does not yield that quantifier. No spanning-circuit clique characterization equivalent to the fixed-code finding was identified in the checked sources.
